With export, it holds file { path, name, bytes }; it also holds health from the shared check. Refused: no element to bring over, or no document. One undo step.
element_to_document.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/cad.py

scan_snapshot_list.description: List the screenshots that the person took with ScanRuler's camera key, newest first, without the pictures. The camera key is the camera on the toolbar, or Alt+Shift+S. No inputs. The answer holds: shots [{ index (0 the newest), id, at (the time), workspace, note (the words of the person), width, height, marks (how many), pins [numbered, with their comments], savedTo }]. Only the person takes a shot; no tool does. No shot is kept in the project unless the person saved it, and they are gone when FreeCAD closes. An empty list means that none was taken yet: ask the person to press the camera key. scan_snapshot_latest shows one. Changes nothing.
scan_snapshot_list.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/snapshot.py

scan_snapshot_latest.description: Show one of the screenshots of the person as a picture, with their marks drawn in. Inputs: index (0, the newest, by default; 1 the one before …) or id (from scan_snapshot_list). original: true gives it as taken, without the marks. The answer holds the picture itself, and index, id, at, workspace, note, width, height, marks, pins, savedTo, of, picture, file. pins: numbered; what the person points at, and what they say of each. of: how many shots there are. picture: "with the marks" or "as taken". Read the note and the pins before the picture: they say what the person wants looked at. Refused (not_found): there is none. Then ask the person to press the camera key (ScanRuler toolbar, or Alt+Shift+S). Refused: index or id names none; the message gives the range. Changes nothing.
scan_snapshot_latest.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/snapshot.py

scan_snapshot_wait.description: Wait for the next screenshot or finished mark-up of the person, then say what scan_snapshot_list says of it. Input: timeout (or timeoutSeconds, the same): seconds, 120 by default, 600 at most. Gotcha: how to call it. A plain call runs on FreeCAD's own thread. There, waiting would hold the window still, so the person could not press the camera key. So a plain call does not wait at all, and it answers came: false, waited: 0 and next. To wait, start it beside the window: job_start { tool: "scan_snapshot_wait", arguments: { timeoutSeconds: 300 }, wait: false }. Tell the person to take the shot. Then job_status { job } reads the answer; give it no long wait of its own, because that holds the window too. Simpler still: ask the person, and call scan_snapshot_latest when they say it is done. The answer holds came: true, with index, id, at, workspace, note, width, height, marks, pins, savedTo and next. Or it holds came: false and a note, when none came in time. A shot still open in the mark-up view does not count until the person finishes it. Changes nothing.
scan_snapshot_wait.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/snapshot.py

reverse_feature_add.description: Add a feature to the list of the Reverse engineer, and rebuild. It goes in at the rollback bar, or right after the feature that after names. feature: one record { kind, name?, …fields }. features: several, added one after another in one step. Read reverse_feature_schema { kind } before you use a kind for the first time: it gives the fields and their defaults. The kinds: [sketch, extrude, revolve, coil, shell, fillet, chamfer, hole, thread, extract, cutPlane, mirror, boolean, sheet, split, loft, sweep, thicken, pattern, offsetBody, moveBody, draft, moveFace, deleteFace, surface, network, trim]. import comes through reverse_import_step. The usual road starts with a sketch on a plane. { kind: "sketch", plane: { kind: "world", axis: "z", offset: 0 }, sketch: { entities: [{ id, kind: "line", a: [x, y], b } | { id, kind: "circle", c, r } | { id, kind: "arc", c, r, start, sweep (radians) }], constraints: [], nextId } }. axis z is the XY plane at Z offset; x is YZ; y is XZ. The plane can also be the plane of a section or a measured plane, which needs that scan open. The sketch is in the millimetres of the sketch plane. Lines that meet at their ends close a region. Then { kind: "extrude", sketchId, extent: { kind: "distance", from: 0, to: 20 }, op: "new" | "join" | "cut" }. You can leave regions out when the sketch has exactly one. Then features on the bodies (fillet, chamfer, shell, hole …), with body (id or name) and their picks. The id of a body is the id of the feature that made it (a further piece: id + n/1024). Its name is the name of that feature. Picks (edges, faces, the face of a thread, the groups of a draft): whole numbers are indices. They are indices into reverse_body_describe { body }, as the body is built NOW. They are stored as fingerprints (kind, place, direction, size, maker), which the build finds again. The indices change with every build. So read them again after every change, and never reuse old ones. You can give a fingerprint object instead. Feature fields can read parameters through exprs: { "extent.to": "h * 2" }. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. It returns once the bodies are rebuilt: read the status of each added row. A feature can be added and still fail to build. It stays in the list, failed, until it is mended, suppressed or removed. The row of a sketch is ok with a note: nothing is built for a sketch alone. Refused, and nothing added: an unknown kind, a name already used, or fields that do not fit the kind. Refused, and nothing added: a feature that is not ready (no closed region, no edges, no body). Refused, and nothing added: an index that the body does not have, or a body that is not built. The answer holds: added, failed [{ id, name, message }], bodies [{ id, name, volume mm³, closed, surface, faces, box }], steps { recomputed, restored, of }, and health. added: the id, name and status of each feature (ok | failed with message | rolledBack). added also holds warning, when a pick was found another way. health is red when a feature failed. The part lives in one FreeCAD object, "Reverse engineer" (ScanRulerReverse). Under it, there is a ReverseBody object for every body; the build writes their shapes. Do not change those objects with other tools. A cut, a fillet or a placement written into a ReverseBody is lost at the next build. Add a feature instead: moveBody moves a body. To work on a body elsewhere, make a copy (part_transform { copy: true }), or export it. Builds run inside FreeCAD and cannot be stopped. A long list is rebuilt from the changed feature on, and earlier steps are kept.

feature.description: The feature as the list stores it (reverse_feature_schema { kind } gives each kind's fields and defaults): kind, and its fields. Picks (edges, faces) are indices from reverse_body_describe or fingerprints.

items.description: The feature as the list stores it (reverse_feature_schema { kind } gives each kind's fields and defaults): kind, and its fields. Picks (edges, faces) are indices from reverse_body_describe or fingerprints.

after.description: A feature: its id, or its name.

reverse_feature_add.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen): plugins/reverse/app/reFeatureCommands.ts (add)

reverse_feature_update.description: Change fields of a feature. feature: id or name. set { field: value, … }: the fields as reverse_feature_add takes them. reverse_feature_list { feature } shows the record as stored. The part is rebuilt from that feature on. kind and id cannot be changed: remove the feature and add the other kind. name must stay unique. suppressed: false brings it back. Bodies can be given by name, and picks by index, as in reverse_feature_add. But mind which body the indices count on. reverse_body_describe shows the body as built now, which already carries the own work of this feature. For example, a filleted edge is no longer there. To pick on the body that the feature starts from, use four calls. reverse_feature_rollback { after: the feature before it } (or top: true), then reverse_body_describe. Then this update, then reverse_feature_rollback {} to build all again. The note of the answer says so whenever indices were given. To change a sketch, set its whole sketch record. exprs: { "radius": "r" } ties a field to a parameter. Setting the number of the field does not remove its expression: set exprs without it. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. The answer holds: feature, result, failed, bodies, steps, note, health. feature: the record as stored now. result: its build row (status, message, warning). Refused: a feature not found. Refused: an empty set. Refused: a changed kind or id, or a taken name. Refused: an index or body that is not there.

feature.description: A feature: its id, or its name.

reverse_feature_update.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen): plugins/reverse/app/reFeatureCommands.ts (update)

reverse_feature_remove.description: Remove a feature (id or name) from the list, and rebuild. A feature that others build on is refused, naming them. Examples: a sketch that an extrude uses, a body that a fillet works on. dependents: true removes them too. To leave it out for a while without losing it, use reverse_feature_suppress instead. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. The answer holds: removed (the ids that went), results, failed, bodies, steps, health. The bodies that it made are gone from the document with it. Body ids of other features do not change.

feature.description: A feature: its id, or its name.

reverse_feature_remove.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen): plugins/reverse/app/reFeatureCommands.ts (remove)

reverse_feature_move.description: Move a feature (feature) or several (features), each by id or name, to just after another (after), and rebuild. Left out, after is the top of the list. Refused, saying which: a feature would then come before something that it builds on. Refused: after is itself one of those moved. The rollback bar stays at the same count from the top. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. The answer holds: results, failed, bodies, steps, health. Check the statuses. A feature that now plays on a different body state can fail, or find its picks another way (warning).

reverse_feature_suppress.description: Suppress a feature (id or name). It is left out of the build, but kept in the list with its fields and picks. suppressed: false brings it back; true is the default. Features that build on a suppressed one fail until it is back; their rows say so. It is the quick way to find which feature breaks a build, or to step past a slow one. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. The answer holds: results (the suppressed feature has no row), failed, bodies, steps, health.

reverse_feature_rollback.description: Move the rollback bar. Only the features above it are built, and reverse_feature_add inserts at it. after: the last feature built (id or name). top: true builds none. Neither (an empty call) rolls all the way down again, and builds everything. Nothing is removed. The features below the bar keep their fields, and read rolledBack in reverse_feature_list. Use it to see the body as it stood before a feature. reverse_body_describe then counts on that state: that is the way to pick the edges of an existing feature again. Use it also to add a feature in the middle. While rolled back, the bodies in the document are those of the built part only. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. The answer holds: rollback { after (the id of the last built feature, or null), built, of }, results, failed, bodies, steps, health.

reverse_feature_clear.description: Take every feature and every parameter away. The part is empty again, and its bodies leave the document. confirm: true is required; without it, the call is refused. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts all of it back. Imported STEP texts stay stored with the container. The answer holds: results [], failed [], bodies [], steps.

reverse_feature_list.description: List the features in order. The answer holds: features [{ id, name, kind, status (ok | failed), message (why it failed), suppressed, rolledBack (below the bar), key { value, unit } (its main number), exprs }], rollback { built, of }, and parameters (how many). A sketch has no status of its own: nothing is built for it alone. feature: one feature (id or name), whole, as stored. That holds every field and its picks as fingerprints, with result (its last build row) or rolledBack. detail: "brief" gives that one as a row. detail: "full" gives every feature whole; that is long, because sketches carry all their entities. Read it after any change that reported a failure, and before reverse_feature_update, to see the field names. Changes nothing.

feature.description: A feature: its id, or its name.

reverse_feature_schema.description: Read the fields of one feature kind as reverse_feature_add takes them. The defaults are those that the box of the panel opens with. kind is one of [sketch, extrude, revolve, coil, shell, fillet, chamfer, hole, thread, extract, cutPlane, mirror, boolean, sheet, split, loft, sweep, thicken, pattern, offsetBody, import, moveBody, draft, moveFace, deleteFace, surface, network, trim]. Another kind is refused with this list. The answer holds: kind, label, fields { name: default }, picks. In fields, null marks what must be given: a body, an axis, a plane. picks: how edges and faces are given. The defaults follow the part as it is now. extrude and revolve offer the last sketch, and its region when it has exactly one. It lists field names, not every allowed value. The kinds of an extent are distance, toPlane, toFace, toBody, betweenPlanes. An op is new, join or cut; the op of a boolean is join, cut, intersect. The axis of a revolve is { kind: "world", axis: "x" | "y" | "z" } or { kind: "sketchLine", entity: id }. Read it before you add a kind for the first time. Changes nothing.

reverse_build.description: Rebuild the part from its feature list, and say how it went. The answer holds: results (the status, message and warning of every built feature), failed, bodies, steps { recomputed, restored, of }, and health. Steps whose inputs did not change are taken from the kept state (restored), not played again. The other reverse tools rebuild by themselves. Use this after a change to a scan, a section or an element that a feature rests on. They are read at build time. Use it also after doc_open, or to read the answer of the whole build. It writes the shapes of the bodies into the document. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. It runs inside FreeCAD and cannot be interrupted; reverse_build_stop is not available in this port. A body of many faces with fillets, shells or patterns can take a long time (not measured).

reverse_build_stop.description: Not available in this port: it is always refused (unavailable). The original stops a hung build by throwing its kernel worker away. Here, builds run inside the own process of FreeCAD, so there is nothing to stop from outside. What to do instead, for a build that answered but was slow: reverse_feature_suppress the slow feature, or reverse_feature_rollback above it. A FreeCAD that no longer answers is Agent Link's to restart (app_force_restart). history_undo afterwards takes the last edit back. Changes nothing.

reverse_parameter_list.description: List the named parameters of the part. The answer holds: parameters [{ id, name, kind (length | angle | integer | number), expression (as written), value, error, comment }]. value: worked out; mm for a length, degrees for an angle. error: when the expression cannot be worked out; then value is null. Features read them through their exprs (reverse_feature_list shows which). The list is empty when there are none. Changes nothing.

reverse_parameter_add.description: Add a named parameter. name: a letter or underscore, then letters, digits, underscores. name must not be a word that the expressions keep: a unit, a constant like pi, a function like sin. name must not differ from another name by capitals alone. expression: a number, or a formula over the other parameters. The formula can use + − × ÷, parentheses, sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 sqrt abs min max floor ceil round pow. kind: length (the default, mm), angle (degrees), integer or number. comment. A feature reads it through exprs: reverse_feature_update { feature, set: { exprs: { "extent.to": "h" } } }. The feature is rebuilt whenever the parameter changes. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. The answer holds: parameter { id, name, kind, expression, value, error? }, results, failed, bodies, steps, health. An expression that cannot be worked out is still added, with its error in the answer: check it. Refused: a name that will not do (the message says why). Refused: an unknown kind, or no expression.

reverse_parameter_set.description: Give a parameter a new expression and/or comment; every feature that reads it is rebuilt. parameter: by name, matched exactly, or by id. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. The answer holds: parameter { id, name, kind, expression, value, error? }, results, failed, bodies, steps, health. Read failed: a new value can make a feature fail (a fillet too large, an extrude of nothing). It stays failed until the value or the feature is changed. Worked example: a block 40 × 30 whose height reads h. It goes from 24000 to 12000 mm³ when h is set from 20 to 10. Refused: a parameter not found; the message lists them.

reverse_parameter_rename.description: Rename a parameter, in every expression and every feature that reads it. parameter: its name or id. to: the new name. Values do not change. The new name follows the rules of reverse_parameter_add. A new name that will not do is refused, saying why. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. The answer holds: results, failed, bodies, steps, health (nothing should change in them).

reverse_parameter_remove.description: Remove a parameter (name or id) that nothing reads. A parameter that an expression or a feature reads is refused, naming the readers. Change them first: reverse_feature_update { set: { exprs: { … } } } without it, or reverse_parameter_set on the parameter that reads it. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. The answer holds: results, failed, bodies, steps, health.

reverse_body_names.description: List the bodies that the build left, as built now (above the rollback bar). The answer holds: bodies [{ id, name, volume, closed, surface, faces, box { min, max }, style { name, color }, visible }]. id: the id of the feature that made it; a further piece of a split is id + n/1024. name: the name of that feature. volume: mm³; 0 for a surface. closed: a closed solid. surface: a sheet, not a solid. faces: the count. box: read off the geometry itself, for a body of up to 400 faces. So a round face reads its true size. Above 400 faces, box is read off its triangulation, and it is a little large. style: what reverse_body_set gave it. The other reverse tools name a body by id, by name, or by its style name. The part lives in one FreeCAD object, "Reverse engineer" (ScanRulerReverse). Under it, there is a ReverseBody object for every body; the build writes their shapes. They are the output of the build. object_list shows them, and measuring, rendering and export tools may read them. But a change made to one by another tool is lost at the next build. An empty list means that nothing is built. That is: no features, the bar at the top, or every feature failed (reverse_feature_list). Changes nothing.

reverse_body_describe.description: List the faces and edges of a body, each with its index and fingerprint. The edges of a fillet, the faces of a shell or the face of a thread are picked by these. body: its id or name. The answer holds: body { id, name, volume, closed, surface, faces, box }, faces and edges. faces [{ index, kind (plane, cylinder, cone, sphere …), centroid, dir, area, radius (round ones), origin }]. dir: the normal of a plane, the axis of a cylinder. origin: the id of the feature that made it. edges [{ index, kind (line, circle, arc …), mid, dir, length, radius, faces, origin }]. faces of an edge: the two faces that it lies between (kind and dir). detail: "brief" gives only the counts. Indices start at 0, and they are NOT FreeCAD's Face1 / Edge1 numbers. FreeCAD's numbers start at 1 and are ordered differently: use these indices only in the reverse tools. They count on the body as it is built now, and they change with every build. So describe again after every change, before you pick. A pick is stored as its fingerprint, which the build finds again. A box has 6 faces and 12 edges. Its four upright edges are the lines whose dir is [0, 0, ±1]. The list is long on a body with many faces. Every edge is listed: several hundred rows on a filleted, patterned part. Take brief first. Changes nothing.

reverse_body_check.description: Check whether a body (id or name) is a valid closed solid, by the own check of the kernel. The answer holds: body (id), name (its feature's), shownAs, closed, valid, solids, shells, volume (mm³), surface (a sheet). shownAs: the name that reverse_body_set gave it, when it has one. closed: a closed solid. valid: OCCT's shape check. solids: the count; more than 1 means pieces that do not touch. shells: per solid; 1 is a plain solid, and 2 or more means a sealed cavity inside. A sound printable body reads closed true, valid true, solids 1. Agent Link's body_check gives a fuller reading (slivers, short edges). It reads the document object of the same body, by its label. Changes nothing.

reverse_body_clearance.description: Read how two bodies stand to each other. a, b: each an id or a name; both must be built. The answer holds: a, b (ids), gap and overlap. gap: the least distance between them, mm; 0 when they touch or overlap. overlap: the volume that they share, mm³; 0 when apart or only touching. gap above 0: clear by that much. gap 0 and overlap 0: touching. overlap above 0: they interfere. Worked example: two blocks whose facing sides are 5 mm apart read gap 5, overlap 0. It is exact (OCCT's distance and common volume). It is slow on bodies with many curved faces (not measured). Changes nothing.

reverse_body_set.description: Name a body, colour it, or show and hide it. body: id or name. Give at least one of name, color and visible. name: its label in the tree of the document. The reverse tools then also find it by that name. Its id and its build name stay. color: #rrggbb, #rgb, or a swatch: red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple. visible: false hides it in the window, and leaves it out of the combined shape of the container. A hidden body is still built, and you can still name it. It is kept with the part, by body id, so it survives rebuilds. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. reverse_import_step.description: Bring a STEP file in as bodies of the Reverse engineer part. It makes a body for every solid in the file, in the frame that the file was drawn in. A file of faces alone comes in as a surface body. Use it for a bought-in part, a mating part, or the CAD model to check the scan against. path: the .step / .stp file. A relative path means the folder of the session, where export { objects, path: "part.step" } writes one. The file must begin as STEP (ISO-10303-21); a mesh or another CAD format is refused. name: the name of the Import feature; it must be unused. By default, it is the name of the file, less its extension. The feature goes in at the rollback bar. The text of the file is stored with the part, so the document no longer needs the file. A large STEP makes a large document. Bodies get the id of the feature (further solids: id + n/1024) and its name. Put them in place with reverse_feature_add { feature: { kind: "moveBody", bodies: [id or name], translate: [x, y, z], rotate: [rx, ry, rz] (degrees), copy: false } }. Combine them with kind boolean. This is not import_file: the bodies belong to the feature list, and they are rebuilt with it. It is one FreeCAD undo step: history_undo puts the list and the bodies back. The answer holds: added [{ id, name, kind, status, bodies }], failed, bodies (all built now, the new ones among them), steps, health. A file with no solid and no surface is added and fails, saying so. OCCT's STEP reader runs inside FreeCAD and cannot be stopped. A file of tens of megabytes can take minutes (not measured).
